facts.text: Marinette was named after Marie Antoinette Chevalier, a Métis trader who ran a post near the Menominee River mouth.
The city sits on the bank of the Menominee River where it empties into Green Bay, and the neighboring city of Menominee, Michigan, lies just across the river.
Marinette’s historic library, the Stephenson Public Library, was donated by a local businessman and now houses a statue of animated film director John Hubley.
Two dozen sawmills once lined the Menominee River, making lumber the backbone of Marinette’s early economy.
The Marinette Logging and Heritage Fest, started in 2012, replaced the old Fourth of July Celebration and features a Sunset Concert Series produced by Theatre on the Bay.
Freight trains now run through Marinette on the Wisconsin Central Ltd line, a legacy of the former Chicago and Northwestern Railway.
